Saved a new skill. The generalizable lesson from this question:

When an OfficeQA OLS question says the predictor is "year (numeric, untransformed)" and asks you to **return the slope AND intercept** (rather than forecast a value), the x-vector must be the literal year numbers (1929...1942), not a 1..N index. The slope is identical either way, but the intercept is not — raw years produce the large negative intercept the gold answer expects (−184.143). The existing forecast skill uses 1..N indexing because the intercept never surfaces there, so it would have led a future agent astray on this variant. The new skill `officeqa-ols-slope-intercept-raw-year` captures the distinction, the verified recipe, and cross-references to the neighboring OLS/regression skills so they don't get confused with each other.

No memory edit needed — my memory is near its char cap and this is fully covered by the new skill.
